rows.narrative_beat: The pair leave the farmhouse before the damp grass dries.
Sigrid checks the smoke direction against the folded map.
Soren notices that the boot prints now overlap the trail rather than lead it.
They exchange a look and continue without explaining the change.
Rainwater feeds a shallow runnel across their path.
Sigrid steps the runnel first and points out an older stone marker.
The marker bears a simple mill-wheel sketch, not a name.
Soren folds the map to hide the farmhouse and expose the creek line.
The trail narrows under wet branches.
Sigrid hears the water before it is visible.
Soren finds a length of soot-stained twine caught on a thorn.
The twine points downhill as if pulled taut and released.
They follow the creek instead of the tracks.
The smoke briefly disappears behind a shoulder of ridge.
Sigrid marks the loss of sight on the map with a wet thumb.
Soren says the smoke must be closer than it looks.
The abandoned mill appears below, roofline broken against pale morning.
Smoke rises from behind the mill rather than from its chimney.
Sigrid signals Soren to stay off the open bridge.
They cross the creek on stones below the bridge.
A freshly tied strip of red cloth moves from a lower branch.
Soren stops Sigrid from touching the cloth.
They circle toward the mill's collapsed loading door.
A thin smoke thread rises from a metal drum hidden behind stone.
The drum contains only wet pine needles and a damp ember.
Sigrid tests the heat without disturbing the ember.
Soren sees a second twine line disappearing through the mill wall.
The line is tied to a small brass bell inside the doorway.
Sigrid chooses the wall opening rather than the doorway.
Inside, daylight bars stripe standing water and broken gears.
Sigrid finds dry footprints ending at the water's edge.
Soren sees the footprints begin again on the far side, facing back.
A quiet drip rings the brass bell once from outside.
Neither moves toward the bell.
Sigrid notices a sealed tin on an upper beam.
Soren reaches it with a fallen plank while Sigrid braces the plank.
The tin holds dry matches, a hand-drawn creek map, and a blank note card.
The map marks the farmhouse with a small square and the mill with a circle.
A third mark is visible upstream, beyond the map edge.
Sigrid decides the smoke was a signal, not a campfire.
The hidden drum finally goes out in the rain.
The bell rings again, now from the creek side.
They leave the tin open on the stone and retreat together.
At the creek, Soren cuts the twine line with a pocket knife.
The distant bell does not ring after the cut.
Sigrid keeps the creek map inside her wrap rather than the notebook.
They climb back toward the farmhouse under a cleared sky.
From the ridge, the farmhouse is visible but its chimney has begun to smoke.
Soren realizes they did not light the stove before leaving.
Sigrid breaks into a run toward the house; Soren follows with the map.
